qs.q: Where do most great startup ideas come from?
o: A cool gadget you saw in a movie
A problem that many people face often
qs.why: Founders start by noticing problems people face again and again.

qs.q: In the R-E-U test, what does "Executable" mean?
o: Our team can build a first version with our skills, time and money
The idea makes money on day one
Nobody has thought of it before
qs.why: Executable asks: can WE actually make a simple first version?

qs.q: Why do we ask "Why?" three times?
o: To find who is to blame
To dig past the symptom to the root cause
qs.why: Each why digs one level deeper, until you reach the real cause.

qs.q: Which hat looks for risks and what could go wrong?
qs.why: The Black hat is the careful critic who spots dangers.

qs.q: How did Zomato begin in 2008?
o: As a website that put restaurant menus online
qs.why: It started as Foodiebay, putting restaurant menus online.

qs.q: What is a "workaround"?
o: The messy fix people use today because no good solution exists
qs.why: Workarounds are a clue that the problem is real and painful.

qs.q: What did teams do in the Chandni Chowk Challenge?
o: Spotted real problems in a busy market and brainstormed solutions
qs.why: It trained your eyes to find problems and turn them into ideas.

qs.q: "A machine that teleports students to school." Which test does it fail first?
qs.why: Teleporting cannot happen in the real world, so it is not realistic.

qs.q: Why is networking useful for a young founder?
o: You meet future co-founders, users and mentors
qs.why: People you meet can become your team, customers and guides.

qs.q: Which hat is about fresh, creative new ideas?
qs.why: Green means growth: new options and creative thinking.

qs.q: Which of these is the strongest problem to build a startup on?
o: Something that happens once a year to one person
Something that happens daily to many people who already use a messy workaround
Something nobody has ever complained about
qs.why: Frequent, widespread, with workarounds: a strong problem.

qs.q: "A photo app exactly like Instagram, with nothing different." Which test does it fail?
qs.why: A copy with nothing new is not unique.

qs.q: What does the White hat focus on?
qs.why: White is neutral: facts and numbers only.

qs.q: What is the Blue hat's job?
o: Managing the thinking: planning, summing up, deciding next steps
qs.why: Blue is the organiser of the whole thinking process.

qs.q: In the Three Why Approach, the first problem you notice is usually...
qs.why: What you see first is a symptom. The whys lead to the root cause.

qs.q: Airbnb began when its founders rented out...
qs.why: In 2007 they rented air mattresses when hotels were full.

qs.q: "Our class builds a full hospital inside school by summer." Which test does it fail?
qs.why: Hospitals exist, but building one is far beyond a student team.

qs.q: Who created the Six Thinking Hats method?
qs.why: Edward de Bono described it in his 1985 book Six Thinking Hats.

qs.q: What is the main rule while brainstorming?
o: Produce many ideas fast, without judging them yet
qs.why: Quantity first; judge and pick later.

qs.q: Wearing the Red hat, you are allowed to...
o: Share feelings and gut reactions without giving reasons
qs.why: Red is for emotions and instincts.
